title: The Hard Ghost
premise: Dominic Marchetti, a deniable fixer for the Meridian Consular Group — an embassy that exists on no map — keeps his crew alive by keeping them invisible. When a realtor's listing exposes their safe house down to the coffee cups on the counter, Dominic realizes someone inside sold them out, and the buyer is a cartel accountant who holds the ledger that could burn every government that employs them. Racing a border checkpoint rotation that will seal their only escape route, Dominic must decide whether to trade the ledger for his crew's lives or expose it and destroy the found family he built. In the end, he trades himself: surrendering to the buyers as bait while his crew walks the ledger across the border, choosing truth over loyalty at the cost of his own freedom.
about_author: Cyrus Nystrom is the pen name of a former logistics contractor who spent nine years moving people and paper across borders he was never cleared to name. He writes thrillers from a coastal town where, he insists, nothing interesting has ever happened.

chapters.title: The House That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. A routine cleanup job in Rotterdam ends with Dominic returning to find the safe house listed online — twelve photos, including the interior, timestamped three days ago. The crew's faces are blurred but the layout isn't. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath practiced calm; invisibility was the whole contract.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV: Wren, the crew's signals analyst. She audits who could have photographed the house and finds the listing agent doesn't exist in any registry. The team argues about whether to run or dig in. Emotional beat: fraying trust; everyone becomes a suspect, and Wren quietly suspects herself first.

chapters.title: Meridian Doesn't Return Calls
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. He contacts the Consular Group's handler, Aldous Vane, who offers extraction for two — not five. Dominic refuses to abandon the crew. Emotional beat: the institution reveals itself as disposable employer; loyalty to people over organization crystallizes.

chapters.title: The Accountant's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Teo, the crew's young driver. He recognizes the interested buyer from the listing traffic: Emil Sarr, a cartel accountant whose encrypted ledger names officials across four governments. Teo once drove for him. Emotional beat: guilt resurfacing; Teo realizes his old life may have led the wolves home.

chapters.title: Twelve Photos, One Mistake
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Frame-by-frame analysis shows a reflection in a hallway mirror — a wristwatch belonging to none of them. Someone entered while they were out. Emotional beat: violation and paranoia tightening like a wire; the house itself feels compromised.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Math
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. The northern border checkpoint rotates guards Thursday at 0600; after that, biometric screening goes live. They have seventy-two hours to move the ledger or themselves. Emotional beat: ticking-clock pressure forcing strategy over instinct; Dominic plans a trade he hasn't told anyone about.

chapters.title: What Teo Knew
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Confronted gently by Dominic, Teo admits Sarr recruited him months ago as an informant — before he defected to the crew. He never gave up the safe house, but he gave up routes. Emotional beat: confession and forgiveness; found family tested and holding.

chapters.title: The Open House
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol, the crew's forger. She poses as a buyer at the listed showing and confirms Sarr's men are casing it, photographing escape routes. She lifts a burner phone from one. Emotional beat: audacity as armor; Marisol's humor masking real fear.

chapters.title: Burner Conversations
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. The stolen phone reveals Sarr's deadline: deliver the ledger's decryption key or the crew's identities go to every agency hunting them. Wren decrypts one message too many and learns Vane is already negotiating against them. Emotional beat: betrayal stacking on betrayal; no clean side left.

chapters.title: The Price List
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. Alone, Dominic reviews what each crew member's exposure would cost — prison, worse — and drafts an offer to Sarr: the key in exchange for passage. He hides it from the others. Emotional beat: the weight of unilateral sacrifice; love expressed as secrecy.

chapters.title: Safe House Siege Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. The crew drills defense scenarios, laughing through the absurdity of fortifying a rented house. Under the laughter, they rehearse goodbye contingencies without saying so. Emotional beat: gallows camaraderie; the family dynamic at its warmest before the break.

chapters.title: Vane's Counteroffer
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. Vane surfaces in person, offering full pardons if Dominic hands over both the ledger AND Teo, the loose end. Dominic declines and lets Vane leave alive — barely. Emotional beat: moral line drawn in blood-adjacent ink; the embassy becomes the enemy.

chapters.title: Sarr in the Flesh
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Sarr requests a meeting through the burner — just him and Teo, old colleagues. Over coffee, Sarr is disarmingly kind, offering Teo his old life back. Teo records everything. Emotional beat: seduction of the past versus the fragile present; Teo chooses, finally, out loud.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Second Lock
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. Cracking deeper into the ledger, Wren discovers it contains Meridian's own operations — Vane's name is in it. The secret worth killing for implicates everyone. Emotional beat: vertigo of scale; truth stops being a weapon and becomes a bomb.

chapters.title: Split Routes
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. The crew votes: split up, two decoy vehicles north, the ledger south with Wren. Marisol volunteers for the decoy run and everyone knows what that means. Emotional beat: courage distributed unevenly and accepted anyway; loyalty made logistical.

chapters.title: Thursday, 0400
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. Two hours before the shift change, Sarr's men hit the safe house early. The decoys draw half; Dominic holds the rest off with smoke and nerve, buying Wren's convoy its head start. Emotional beat: controlled chaos; Dominic's competence as an act of care.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint Shifts
chapters.summary: POV: Wren. At 0600 the new guard rotation arrives mid-crossing. Wren talks her way through using a forged credential Marisol built for a dead woman — herself, years ago. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into poise; survival as performance.

chapters.title: Trade at the Salt Flats
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. Cornered, Dominic meets Sarr alone and offers the key — plus himself, as insurance Sarr can hand to Meridian to close the file. Sarr accepts. Emotional beat: the sacrifice revealed; Dominic trading his freedom for his family's future.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Says About Me
chapters.summary: POV: Teo. Safe across the border, Teo reads Wren's decrypted files and finds Dominic's drafted offer from Chapter 10 — he'd planned this all along. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude colliding; understanding arriving too late to stop it.

chapters.title: The Crew That Wouldn't Scatter
chapters.summary: POV: Marisol. Instead of dispersing per plan, the crew regroups and votes unanimously: they don't abandon Dominic. They leak the ledger's most damning page to three newspapers simultaneously, making Dominic worthless as a scapegoat. Emotional beat: loyalty weaponized as truth; the theme resolved in action.

chapters.title: Exposure
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic. Headlines detonate. Sarr, suddenly radioactive, releases Dominic rather than be tied to him; Vane is recalled to face inquiry. Dominic walks out of a warehouse into rain, free and unemployed. Emotional beat: release after compression; victory that tastes like ash and relief.

chapters.title: A House With Windows
chapters.summary: POV: Dominic (closing). Months later, the five rent a shabby seaside cottage — listed openly, curtains open, names on the mailbox. They are ghosts no longer, and poorer for it, and glad. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; the price of survival paid, the family intact, visibility chosen at last.
